analysis:
This batch only removes personal data from log lines and adds regression tests. I found no concrete security regression.

Changes examined:
- coordinator/api/device_auth.go: handleDeviceApprove no longer logs user.Email in 'device approved' (base around line 187). It still logs user_code and account_id. Authentication, expiry, status checks and token issuance are unchanged. handleDeviceToken still consumes no code and issues tokens on repeated polls; that is pre-existing (T-039) and not changed here.
- coordinator/api/provider.go: line 146 drops r.RemoteAddr from 'provider websocket connected'. Around line 3391, serial_number is dropped from the attestation-result log. Registration, attestation and trust logic are untouched in the hunks shown. The base text was truncated, so the rest of the file was not reviewed.
- coordinator/api/log_personal_data_test.go (new, test only): captures all log output and asserts that email, remote IP, X-Forwarded-For and device UDID do not appear. It also asserts that account_id does appear. It exercises /v1/admin/credit, /v1/device/approve, /v1/mdm/webhook (accepted and rejected) and /v1/admin/state-export.

Cross-file assumptions for the next pass:
- The test expects other, unsupplied changes to the admin credit handler, the MDM webhook handler, the state-export handler and loggingMiddleware. It also depends on the helpers seedUser, withUser and envStateExportEnabled. Those files are not in this batch and were not verified.
- Removing serial_number and remote address from coordinator logs slightly reduces forensic correlation. The account_id and provider_id identifiers remain, so this is an acceptable privacy trade-off. It aligns with T-051 and T-058 on identity leakage through logs/diagnostics.
